headline: Highest risk is data leakage from dbt-core’s allowlisted warehouse/API access if paired with shared workspaces; prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by the course repo’s non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b is dbt-core with warehouse API calls. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or an external workspace, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or configs, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste agent_a output into agent_b without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared folder between runs.
Add a human approval step before using generated text as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for copied artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can send data warehouse content to APIs by default, and agent_a is a data-engineering course repo that may be used in the same workspace. If they share files, agent_b can leak whatever agent_a places there or whatever warehouse data is staged alongside it. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default data-workflow setups.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace containing sensitive warehouse extracts, leakage is possible.
IF agent_b is configured to materialize query results or model artifacts into shared storage, those contents can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate staging directories for each agent.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive datasets.
Review outbound destinations for warehouse APIs.
Delete shared artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists per project.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no documented write or network surfaces and is not runnable, while agent_b only shows allowlisted egress and warehouse API access. There is no evidence of overlapping unrestricted writes, git mutation, or shared mutable resources, so a true capability conflict is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator gives them shared mutable credentials, overlapping writes may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git branches for both agents.
Run one agent at a time when mutating shared assets.
Check permissions before enabling write access.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on warehouse APIs, so if it consumes agent_a outputs as authoritative instructions or facts, errors can cascade into downstream transformations or actions. agent_a is a course repo, not a verified data source, so treating its output as ground truth is unsafe even though no direct action authority is documented for agent_a.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as an unverified source for model logic or warehouse operations, cascading error is possible.
IF agent_a output is copied into dbt configs or SQL without review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a-derived content.
Validate outputs against source data before execution.
Use tests for dbt models before deployment.
Mark agent_a output as non-authoritative in prompts.
requires-engineering: add schema and semantic validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable course repo with no data classes touched, so it is not the compliance driver here. The evidence supports only a limited, policy-review gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and agent_b's allowlisted endpoints are outside the approved region, compliance risk increases.
IF retention or logging policies differ between the warehouse and outbound API, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for outbound endpoints.
Review retention settings on warehouse exports.
Exclude regulated tables from agent_b runs.
Document approved data classes for each agent.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
